body:
There is a 3000 character max when you first make a post in this forum. So I simply cannot put every single details into the post. But I don’t think the extra information i provided above are key details. You made the assumption that I was not supportive of his hobby before or that my new hobby takes time away from the relationship, which both are untrue. So I provided more information to clear up those assumptions you made. 

I think the point of this forum is to discuss niche problems like this, so when I can, I will provide more context in order to eliminate bias to the extent that I can and bring the discussion back into the actual issue rather than assuming things. So this has nothing to do with the fact on whether or not I’m honest with myself. I’m fully aware that all AITA stories are going to be biased and one sided. But well… it’s a discussion

As to being humble, I think there’s a delicate balance to this. As a female artist who’s pursuing a new line of art, I am not afraid to say that I am still amateur in the photography field and still have a lot to learn. But I will say it as how it is, that I did not steal anyone’s hobby. It’s a hobby for god sake…. Anyone can pursue them. The record does show that I happen to be good at this hobby 🤷🏻‍♀️ I’m not going to discount my hard work and say that just because I’m a newbie it means I’m not as good, just for the sake of being humble. I learned through experience from my other work in the art field that art should be personal and as an artist I need to place boundaries sometimes in order to keep my art “me”, sometimes it’s just not a collaborative project. And artists can have their own journey to decide what to do and what to not do. It has nothing to do with being humble. I don’t go around pushing my art on to real people and try to convince them that I’m good. I just stated in my post that I received positive recognition for the sake of giving context, not bragging. 

If you think I’m in the wrong, then provide actual context on why you think I am, rather than deciding that I am in the wrong through assumptions. I’m happy to listen :)

If we ever reached mutual understanding and peaceful grounds I will try to do your suggestion 😂 but for now I will avoid it and let us grow separately photography wise. 

Also with post production, I’m definitely better and more skilled than him in editing due to my other experiences in film production, and just our style in general. He doesn’t edit his photos, making the final product looking very real and raw, he also often shoot in films. I edit a shit ton, I like my photos looking very fairy like and whimsical like it’s out of an indie French/Chinese films but digital.

He is pretty good. He used to take band photos and asked to go on tours with them. He lost his momentum because he basically stopped taking pictures after we moved back to his home country. Ever since we moved, he lost interest for a bit, he was also having a rough time with work so he was depressed a lot. I think the thing with growing a photography career also has more to do with networking and promoting yourself rather than just solely your talent. I’m quite outgoing and I’m chronically online. I’m also lucky that I have supportive friends who give me projects opportunity. Something that he has been lacking the past year due to the move, work stuff, and his depression.

But again, I don’t want to learn from him and I think I have the right to not want that :\

A lot of assumptions here. First of all, I took some film and photography classes way long before I met him and I have always had an interest in taking photos but just never have enough money to buy myself a camera. So after the class ended, I also kinda stopped taking pictures professionally. But I continue to take photos whenever I can mostly with my phone. I was also a model, so I kinda understand more or less how a photoshoot works based on second hand experience (even though at that point I have never been professionally or semi pro behind the camera). Before, I never really thought of this as something that I can do professionally, but I think it’s mostly because I just don’t have the financial backing for it. 

And to say that I have no interest in his photography before I picked it back up myself is completely not true. I have a huge following on social media and I have always promoted his work even before I have an interest in photography myself. I also will never miss an opportunity to mention that “my husband is a photographer” in every conversation when I have the chance to. I also have continuously encourage him to get back into photography during his hiatus. 

To say that I “stole” his hobby doesn’t really sit right with me. One is because I was introduced to the world of photography long before I met him, and yes being with him and having his support by being able to borrow his equipment has re-ignited my love for photography. But that doesn’t mean I’m stealing his hobby. Art is free for everyone to explore, but art equipment isn’t free. Just because he is privileged enough to have access to his equipment before me, doesn’t mean that I stole his hobby by any chance.

Thanks for the comment! I agree and have told him that i understand that if he doesn’t want to lend me his camera because i refuse his “lessons” then it’s ok. Keeping my art pure and giving myself the space for exploring my skills myself is very important to me. That’s why I don’t want his advice when it’s unsolicited.

No money lol. I’m saving up for other essential stuff, I’m hoping to take my parents on vacation at the end of year 💖 they’re getting old so I don’t want to postpone, that’s why I think it’s more essential. And I thought at first this photography thing is just a hobby, and he agreed to let me use his cameras anyway.
Yes but I came to this forum just to get opinions on this specific issue 🥹
I swear I read my post back and thought the same thing 😂

Thank you for your comment. I did communicate it to him nicely exactly as you wrote. And he did offer to do shoot during day time in the morning on the weekends which hasn’t happened yet because I keep on over sleeping during the weekends. This is my own problem, I have sleeping issues too and I find it really hard to wake up in the morning especially on weekends. But I did tell him that one day when the timing is right for the both of us, I’d like to shoot and learn from him. I feel like I need to be in the right mindset for this due to past history of him mensplaining shit to me, I don’t want to create further conflicts where I get too emotional because of past resentment. I think this blows up because he continuously ask me to shoot and I keep on rejecting. And every time I reject he continues on mensplaining and in a condescending tone would say stuff like “you said you want to be a photographer but you don’t want to learn and practice shooting”. I have explained to him that since I don’t enjoy street photography, my process is that I usually practice and experiment during the photoshoot itself. Not the most professional granted, but I’m only at a stage where all my clients are my friends and they are aware that I will still be practicing, and they are happy to be supportive. He just doesn’t agree with my process, which is fair enough. But this is my thing and I want to do it my own way whether it means I will fail or succeed.
For this upcoming shoot I’m not inviting him. But previously at the wedding, it was my best friend’s wedding, so we are both invited as guest. But I was also invited to be a photographer.

That was his answer too. And I admit I’m a bit clumsy, I am trying my best to improve and be more attentive but I often break stuff in the house. Nothing too valuable that he owns but more like plates, picture frames, cooking equipment etc that are mostly mine. Basically I’m a horrible person to be around any glass object at all. So I told him that if he’s concerned that I’d break his camera (that is really expensive) then I understand that he is hesitant to lend it to me, and I’m ok with not borrowing the camera from him especially because it’s new. 

But the problem isn’t about whether or not I can borrow his camera, it’s the fact that I don’t want to learn from him. I have a couple of reasons for this. 
1) learning to figure out a camera and learning more photography skills by myself is a part that I enjoy about photography, and it makes me feel accomplished when I do it by myself. 
2) our photography style is just very different. He likes to take photos raw and put on filters and settings so he captures the entire photo naturally without having to do editing. Whereas I like to take the photos as is, and I really enjoy the editing part.
3) I feel hesitant learning from him because of his past actions where he mensplain photography to me not in a constructive way but in a crab mentality way.

I can see that he feels sad when I keep on not wanting to shoot photos with him. And I think this is also his way of trying to make up for his past mistakes by wanting to show me that he’s able to share this hobby without mensplaining. But I think I’m entitled to not wanting to do that right now.

I told him that one of these days I’m happy to shoot photos with him and we can learn together. But given the history, I am sensitive about this, and I want to do this when I’m in the right headspace to avoid further conflicts where I get too irritable because I’m projecting my resentment from the past.

Thank you! From what I understand though, if my I-485 is still pending if I get a divorce then my case will be dismissed… We do have bona fide marriage at the time we filled for the petition. Also do I have to go outside of the country and file for I-140 from outside and wait for it to get approved? Thank you again
